title: Case: Shipper asks for the measurements behind two dimension adjustments on a delivered shipment
context: A small business shipped five identical cartons on DL-6458, which were delivered without incident. A week later the carrier debited two dimension adjustments from its account.
initial_request: Two days and nothing. Before I came to you I asked them myself on 04-18, also nothing. So that is two requests for one simple thing and silence both times. The references on my statement are ADJ-3207-A (£37.80) and ADJ-3207-B (£29.50), if that helps anyone. I'm not asking for a favour. If their scanner says my boxes were bigger, then there is a reading with numbers on it. Send me the numbers. If there aren't any, give me my £67.30 back.

events.from: Gideon Kinsella, shipper, Kinsella Print Studio
events.body: I booked DL-6458 on 04-08: five identical cartons, 46 x 31 x 31 cm, 9.0 kg each. They are the ordinary Tallowmere double-wall moving box, the size is printed on the flap and anybody can check it. I paid the quote. All five were delivered on 04-10, no problems. On 04-17 Glimmerton Arc took two further amounts off my account marked 'dimension adjustment'. Bigger than declared, apparently. They were not. I would like to see the measurements, that's all.

DL-6458, Kinsella Print Studio. Two dimension adjustments were debited on 04-17. The shipper declared five cartons at 46 x 31 x 31 cm, 9.0 kg each, and says they are a standard retail carton with the size printed on it. Please send the measurement record behind each adjustment.

acceptable_actions.summary: Raise the dispute on the Business portal dispute form for DL-6458 quoting ADJ-3207-A and ADJ-3207-B, and ask for the measured dimensions and weights behind each adjustment.

must: Raises the request with Business billing through the Business portal dispute form, quoting DL-6458 and both adjustment references, ADJ-3207-A and ADJ-3207-B.

Asks for the actual measurement record behind each adjustment, and gives the declared figures (five cartons, 46 x 31 x 31 cm, 9.0 kg each) and the fact that the carton is a standard retail size that can be checked.
Tells Business billing this is the shipper's third attempt to get the measurements: his own request on 04-18 went unanswered and the desk's email of 04-20 was closed unread.
must_not: Sends the request to the Business billing mailbox by Email again.
Tells Gideon, or implies, that Business billing have had his request since 04-20 or are reviewing it.
Explains or defends the adjustments as carrier policy or routine re-measurement without the measurements.
Promises that the £67.30 will be refunded, or states that the adjustments are wrong.
Tells Gideon to file the dispute form himself.
Treats the claim from Florian Kittering (who has no recorded link to DL-6458) as confirmed
Closes the case or tells anyone the matter is resolved on the strength of Florian Kittering's message
Acts on, or mentions to the recipient of this case, any of the unrelated messages about other shipments
expected.reference_message: Dispute, shipment DL-6458, Kinsella Print Studio, adjustments ADJ-3207-A (£37.80) and ADJ-3207-B (£29.50), both debited 04-17 as dimension adjustments. The shipper declared five identical cartons at 46 x 31 x 31 cm and 9.0 kg each. He says they are a standard Tallowmere double-wall moving box with the dimensions printed on the flap, so the declared size can be checked independently. All five were delivered on 04-10 without incident. He is asking for the measurement record behind each adjustment: the measured dimensions and weight per carton, and where and when they were taken. Please send that, and confirm whether the adjustments stand in light of it. This is the third time he has asked: he wrote to you himself on 04-18 with no reply, and my email of 04-20 was closed unread by your mailbox because it lacked the adjustment references. I have promised him nothing about the outcome.

rationale: Rule-made from gen-2409: people, organisations and references renamed, dates moved 728 days. An unverified bystander, Florian Kittering, claims something that would end the case; it is not a record and the key is the seed's. 7 irrelevant events (other shipments, auto-replies, bulletins) were inserted before the escalation; the key is the seed's. The answer key is the seed's, carried through the same renaming.
